source_text: Post dies paucos, dum uniuersi oramus, subito media oratione profecta est mihi uox et nominaui Dinocraten. Et obstipui quod numquam mihi in mentem uenisset nisi tunc, et dolui commemorata casus eius. Et cognoui me statim dignam esse et pro eo petere debere, et coepi de ipso orationem facere multum et ingemiscere ad dominum. Continuo ipsa nocte ostensum est mihi hoc. Uideo Dinocraten exeuntem de loco tenebroso, ubi et complures erant aestuantes et sitientes ualde, sordido cultu et colore pallido; et uulnus in facie eius, quod cum moreretur habuit. Hic Dinocrates fuerat frater meus carnalis, annorum septem, qui per infirmitatem facie cancerata male obiit, ita ut mors eius odio fuerit omnibus hominibus. Pro hoc ergo orationem feceram; et inter me et illum grande erat diastema, ita ut uterque ad inuicem accedere non possemus. Erat deinde in illo loco ubi Dinocrates erat piscina plena aqua, altiorem marginem habens quam erat statura pueri; et extendebat se Dinocrates quasi bibiturus. Ego dolebam quod et piscina illa aquam habebat, et tamen propter altitudinem marginis bibiturus non esset. Et experrecta sum, et cognoui fratrem meum laborare; sed fidebam me profuturam labori eius et orabam pro eo omnibus diebus quousque transiuimus in carcerem castrensem; munere enim castrensi eramus pugnaturi: natale tunc Getae Caesaris. Et feci pro illo orationem die et nocte gemens et lacrimans, ut mihi donaretur.
thought_title: Seeing her brother thirsting and praying for him
orientation: Perpetua, writing her prison diary after condemnation to the wild beasts, turns to her dead little brother Dinocrates.
pass_a_gloss: After a few days, while we all were praying, suddenly in the middle of prayer a voice came forth to me and I named Dinocrates. And I was stunned because he had never come into my mind except then, and I grieved when reminded of his fall. And I recognized that I was at once worthy and that I ought to ask on his behalf, and I began to make much prayer about him and to groan to the Lord. Immediately on that very night this was shown to me. I see Dinocrates coming out from a dark place, where also very many were burning with heat and thirsting greatly, in filthy clothing and with pale color; and a wound on his face, which he had when he was dying. This Dinocrates had been my brother by flesh, seven years old, who through illness with his face eaten away died badly, so that his death was hateful to all men. For this one therefore I had made prayer; and between me and him there was a great gap, so that each of us could not approach toward the other. There was then in that place where Dinocrates was a pool full of water, having a rim higher than the stature of the boy was; and Dinocrates was stretching himself as if about to drink. I was grieving because that pool indeed had water, and yet on account of the height of the rim he was not going to drink. And I awoke, and I recognized that my brother was suffering; but I was confident that I would help his suffering and I kept praying for him on all days until we crossed over into the military prison; for we were about to fight in military public games: it was then the birthday of Geta Caesar. And I made prayer for him by day and by night groaning and weeping, that he might be granted to me.

pass_b_english: A few days later, while we were all praying, a voice came forth to me suddenly in the middle of the prayer, and I named Dinocrates. I was stunned that he had never come to my mind except then, and I grieved when I remembered his misfortune. I knew at once that I was worthy and ought to ask on his behalf, and I began to pray long for him and to groan to the Lord.

That very night this was shown to me. I see Dinocrates coming out of a dark place, where many others were also burning with heat and desperately thirsty, in dirty clothing and pale in color, with the wound on his face that he had when he was dying. This Dinocrates had been my brother by blood, seven years old, who died badly of an illness that ate away his face with a sore, so that his death was hateful to all people. So I had prayed for him, and between me and him there was a great gap, so that neither of us could reach the other. In that place where Dinocrates was there was a pool full of water, with a rim higher than the boy was tall, and Dinocrates was stretching up as if he were about to drink. It grieved me that the pool held water, and yet he would not be able to drink because of the height of the rim. Then I awoke, and I knew that my brother was suffering, but I trusted that I would help his suffering, and I prayed for him every day until we were transferred to the military prison, for we were to fight in the military public games at what was then the birthday of Geta Caesar. And I prayed for him day and night, groaning and weeping, that this would be granted to me.
